cards.name: Sticker cut-out with white outline and drop shadow
cards.summary: The subject cut out of its photo with a thick white sticker border and a soft shadow, so it looks like a die-cut sticker lifted off the page.
use_for: social posts and stories with a cut-out subject
avoid: thin, wispy edges (hair, fur): a white outline makes the mask flaws obvious; refine the mask or simplify the outline
a busy background colour close to white: the border disappears; add a darker backdrop
cutter (die-cut) files: they need a real vector path, so use the Illustrator or CorelDRAW plan and expand the result

Setup (script): a pale backdrop; a 62-point polygon that follows the silhouette of the left subject (its outline down to the picture's lower edge); the points were measured against the photo offline, because CorelDRAW has no automatic subject selection (a real job draws the path with the Pen or Bezier tool, or traces a mask); a white copy of it; the photo placed inside the polygon with AddToPowerClip so only the cut-out shows; the cut-out and its white copy are moved to the page centre and scaled to 88 percent so the border and shadow have room.
Contour outside on the white copy behind the cut-out: one step, 0.3 in (about 29 px at 1920, a thick die-cut border), white fill and outline, round corners: the sticker border.
Break Apart on the contour group: the live contour becomes a plain curve, so the shadow follows the outer edge of the border (a shadow on the live group follows only the inner copy).

cards.name: Background blur (portrait-mode bokeh)
cards.summary: The subject stays sharp while the background goes softly out of focus with bright highlights blooming into bokeh discs, like a wide-aperture lens.
use_for: portraits shot on a phone or at a small aperture
product shots with a distracting background
making space for type behind the subject
avoid: a background so close to the subject that real blur would be small: heavy blur looks fake; keep Iris Radius modest
hair and fine edges: blur bleeds the subject into the background unless the subject is removed from the blurred copy first (the Content-Aware step below)
news photos: faking depth of field is an edit; disclose it if required

steps.note: Setup (script): a duplicate of the photo sent behind the original; this copy gets the blur.
Gaussian Blur at the maximum radius (250) on the duplicate behind. One pass is only a light blur on this 1920 px photo (a first run showed it), so the next step repeats it.

The same Gaussian Blur applied 15 more times by script (Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect, radius 250 each): 16 passes in all, because a single pass of the largest radius is only light on a 1920 px photo; the passes compound until the background and the second subject are only soft colour shapes.

steps.script:
import random
from PIL import Image
s.StretchEx(PW / 2, PH / 2, 1.06, 1.06)
im = Image.open("media/plate_photo.png").convert("L").crop((0, 0, 1920, 880)).resize((480, 220))
px = im.load()
cand = [(x * 4, y * 4) for y in range(220) for x in range(480) if px[x, y] > 205 and not (130 < x < 235)]
rnd = random.Random(11)
rnd.shuffle(cand)
chosen = []
for x, y in cand:
    if all((x - a) ** 2 + (y - b) ** 2 > 90 ** 2 for a, b in chosen):
        chosen.append((x, y))
    if len(chosen) >= 26:
        break
for x, y in chosen:
    r = rnd.choice((22, 30, 40, 52, 66)) / PX
    d = layer.CreateEllipse2(x / PX, PH - y / PX, r)
    d.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#FFF3D6"))
    d.Outline.Width = 0.012
    d.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(rgb("#FFFFFF"))
    d.Transparency.ApplyUniformTransparency(72)
print("bokeh discs:", len(chosen))
result = s
steps.note: Bokeh (script): the blurred copy is first scaled up 6 percent so its blurred edges fall off the page; the brightest spots of the photo outside the subject (found with PIL on the plate, seeded) each get a soft pale disc of 22 to 66 px radius at 72 percent transparency with a thin white rim, over the blurred copy and under the sharp subject: the highlights bloom into lens discs. CorelDRAW has no lens-blur or bokeh effect, so the discs are drawn vectors.

Cut-out: a 62-point polygon that follows the silhouette of the left subject (its outline down to the picture's lower edge); the points were measured against the photo offline, because CorelDRAW has no automatic subject selection (a real job draws the path with the Pen or Bezier tool, or traces a mask); the sharp original photo is placed inside it (AddToPowerClip), over the blurred copy and the bokeh discs.

avoid: over-saturating skin: keep Vibrance (not Saturation) for the boost
outline colours that match the background: pick a contrasting outline (white or yellow on dark, black on light)
text over the face: place type beside the subject, never across it

cards.name: Hard offset shadow (pop sticker)
cards.summary: A solid, unblurred shadow offset down-right behind a cut-out, logo or type: the flat comic / pop-art sticker look.
use_for: bold social graphics and promo tiles
cut-out subjects on flat colour backgrounds
avoid: photographic or soft lighting scenes: a hard shadow looks graphic, not real
very long offsets on small items: they read as a second object

effects.note: Layer Style > Drop Shadow on the type layer: Multiply #1A1A1A, 100 %, Spread 100, Size 0, Distance 40 px at 135 degrees (14 px in the first run was only a thicker outline).
